analysis.title: GS US Daily Download 5 Oct 2026
key_insights: Q3 2026 earnings season starts the week of October 12, with about 70% of S&P 500 market cap reported by end of October. Most hyperscalers report in the last week of October.
Consensus expects S&P 500 Q3 y/y EPS growth of 27%, against realized growth of 33% in Q2 excluding some accounting distortions. GS expects most companies to beat consensus again.

AI infrastructure beneficiaries account for over 50% of expected S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116%. For the median S&P 500 stock, consensus y/y EPS growth slows from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3.

Input costs should limit sequential margin expansion in Q3 and the dollar is a smaller tailwind to revenue growth than in Q2. Offsetting that, recent growth data are strong, revision breadth is positive, and tariff refunds ($77B in Q2, $69B in Q3) add roughly 6% of US corporate pre-tax profits each quarter.

Semis 3Q preview: GS sees upside to estimates across most sub-sectors after the sector fell (SOX down 11% vs SPX up 4%) on de-risking. This is a more constructive setup than the cautious tactical stance GS took before 2Q results.

Semis detail: GS expects significant positive revisions for SemiCap on WFE pull-ins and visibility into 2028, upside in server CPUs and key ASIC programs from higher hyperscaler capex, and upside in analog (prefers industrial, aero/defense and datacenter exposure). In memory/storage GS prefers HDDs and NAND because near-term supply additions are lacking.

Banks 3Q preview: investors will focus on capital markets after a strong 2Q (equities trading normalizing QoQ, weaker FICC, a much slower investment banking quarter though still up YoY), NII (strong loan growth and fixed-rate asset repricing offset by higher deposit costs), and slower capital deployment.

Bank valuation looks fair after a 5% share price decline in 3Q26 from multiple derating. GS expects attractive ROTCEs near term, but a re-rating depends on macro clarity and the shape of the rates curve. Best positioned stocks are WFC (on the Conviction List), BAC and C.

Boeing: a union contract ratification reduces the risk of a drawn-out labor dispute and a 777X delay. The FAA declared the 737 MAX software issue not a flight-safety risk, and the F/A-XX win alongside F-47 bolsters the defense growth outlook. GS is Buy rated.

Market color: NDX hit a new all-time high but rates, which backed up to pre-softer-NFP levels, kept risk appetite in check. Asset manager and HF flows were balanced on the week, with Semis demand rising on positive catalysts (solid MU earnings, NVDA's larger buyback plans).
The S&P is down seven straight weeks while concentration into Tech increased in September. HFs rotated into TMT in September while nearly every other sector was net sold.

There is minimal willingness to chase the move higher despite light positioning. Activity is spotty given performance challenges, a more demanding macro backdrop (oil, rates), the midterm overhang and fast narrative shifts within AI.
Light catalyst calendar this week: ISM Services Monday, FOMC Minutes Wednesday, and earnings from STZ (Tuesday night), APLD (Wednesday night), PEP (Thursday morning) and DAL (Friday morning).

sector_views.rationale: Upside to 3Q estimates across most sub-sectors and a more constructive trading setup after the 11% SOX pullback. Prefers SemiCap, analog, HDDs and NAND.
Valuation looks fair at about the 50th percentile of its history and 60% of the S&P 500 multiple. Fundamentals are supportive, but a re-rating needs clarity on macro and the rates curve.
The Boeing F/A-XX award, paired with F-47, bolsters the long-term growth outlook for the defense business.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth: consensus est +27% y/y, versus realized +33% in Q2 excluding some accounting distortions. GS expects most companies to surpass consensus estimates.
Median S&P 500 stock: consensus est y/y EPS growth of 9% in Q3, down from 14% in Q2.
AI infrastructure beneficiaries are estimated to account for over 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3, with hyperscaler capex growth est at 116%.
Tariff refunds totaled $77B in Q2 and $69B in Q3, roughly 6% of total US corporate pre-tax profits each quarter. The private equity stake distortion should fade in Q3.

Banks 3Q26: GS expects 3Q equities trading to normalize QoQ, FICC pockets of weakness, and a much slower investment banking quarter that is still up YoY. NII is supported by loan growth and asset repricing, partly offset by higher deposit costs.
Semis 3Q: GS expects significant positive estimate revisions for SemiCap companies on WFE spending pull-ins, with upside for server CPUs, key ASIC programs and analog.

Reported in the past week: solid MU earnings and NVDA's increased buyback plans drove Semis demand. Upcoming reports: STZ (Tue night), APLD (Wed night), PEP (Thu morning), DAL (Fri morning). Large-cap bank earnings start the week of October 12.

risk_factors: Rates: yields backed up to pre-softer-NFP levels, with very few buyers of duration, and kept risk appetite in check.
Oil and rates make the macro backdrop more demanding.
Input cost pressures could limit sequential margin expansion in Q3.
Bank capital deployment could moderate on lower excess capital, the AOCI impact from higher rates, and three consecutive years of G-SIB buffer increases.
Narrow market leadership concentrated in Tech and AI, with fast-moving AI narratives.
vol_and_positioning: HFs rotated into TMT stocks in September while nearly every other sector was net sold.
Positioning is light, but there is minimal willingness to chase the move higher.
Asset manager and HF flows finished the week balanced, with the one notable flow being a pickup in Semis demand.
The S&P is down seven straight weeks, which GS reads as continued concentration into Tech at the expense of other sectors.
geopolitical: Looming US midterm election overhang is cited as a drag on market activity.

tension_points.bull_case: Large cap banks should keep generating attractive ROTCEs near term on a strong revenue environment and benign credit outlook, and the group trades at about the 50th percentile of its history and 60% of the S&P 500 multiple.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital deployment is likely to moderate on lower excess capital, the AOCI hit from higher rates and three years of G-SIB buffer increases. 3Q has weaker FICC and a much slower investment banking quarter.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A re-rating depends on greater clarity around the macro and the shape of the rates curve in particular.
